posts.summary: A read-only check of your Entra tenant against Microsoft's Entra operations reference guide: sync, licensing, MFA, Conditional Access, consent, privileged roles and PIM, access reviews, recommendations. Run it in…
posts.purpose:
A read-only check of your Microsoft Entra tenant against Microsoft's Microsoft Entra operations reference guide, with a score per area and a fix for every finding. A skill reads the tenant live through the Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise, so there's no script to run: ask Copilot Cowork or GitHub Copilot in VS Code.

Microsoft's guide has four sections. The report has one area for each, and every finding names the guide section it comes from. The full rule list is in rules.md.
needs: Microsoft 365 Copilot with Copilot Cowork, if you run it there instead of PowerShell
gets: A scored HTML report with a fix for every finding, tied to the guide section it comes from

A skill reads the tenant live through the Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise, so there's no script to run: ask Copilot Cowork or GitHub Copilot in VS Code.

It complements the Entra ID Operations Report. That one checks day-to-day operations against Microsoft's operations guide; this one checks attack paths against CISA, CIS and incident guidance. Some checks appear in both (legacy authentication, consent, PIM); run both if you can.
needs: Microsoft 365 Copilot with Copilot Cowork, if you run it there instead of PowerShell

posts.title: Introducing Agent and Tools Cleanup
posts.summary: Finds agents, plugins, skills and MCP servers nobody uses, plus stale agent identities and blueprints. Can block or disable them.
posts.purpose:
Both scripts use only Connect-MgGraph and Invoke-MgGraphRequest (module Microsoft.Graph.Authentication) against Graph beta, and work in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.

Microsoft doesn't document every elementTypes value for plugins yet. Check the elementTypes column in Packages.csv the first time you run it, and tell me if a tool shows up as App.
needs: Microsoft 365 Copilot with Copilot Cowork, if you run it there instead of PowerShell

Microsoft Graph permissions: AgentIdentity.Read.All, AgentIdentityBlueprint.Read.All, AgentIdentityBlueprintPrincipal.Read.All, Application.Read.All, AuditLog.Read.All, AuditLogsQuery.Read.All, CopilotPackages.Read.All, CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All and 1 more
gets: A list of what to remove, and an undo file for anything it changes

posts.title: Introducing Agent and Tools Health Check
posts.summary: A read-only check of agents, tools, Entra agent identities and blueprints against best practices: groups, sponsors, least privilege, clear names, stale items.
posts.purpose:
A read-only check of how well your Copilot agents and tools, Entra agent identities and agent identity blueprints are set up, with a score per area and a fix for every finding. It works like the Copilot Billing Health Check: run it in Copilot Cowork, or from PowerShell.

Based on Microsoft's Entra Agent ID best practices: every agent has a sponsor and an owner, a clear name and description, least-privilege permissions, group-scoped access and Conditional Access, and gets reviewed when it stops being used. The full rule list is in rules.md.
needs: Microsoft 365 Copilot with Copilot Cowork, if you run it there instead of PowerShell

Microsoft Graph permissions: AgentIdentity.Read.All, AgentIdentityBlueprint.Read.All, AgentIdentityBlueprintPrincipal.Read.All, Application.Read.All, AuditLog.Read.All, CopilotPackages.Read.All, Group.Read.All, Policy.Read.All and 2 more
gets: A scored HTML report with a fix for every finding, mapped to CIS and CISA guidance

posts.summary: A read-only check of your Copilot spending policies, their groups and their members. Run it in PowerShell or Copilot Cowork.

A plan for a health check that reviews Microsoft 365 Copilot billing policies and spending policies, the groups they use and the people in those groups. It reports problems and tells you how each policy should be set up.

Status: proof of concept. Get-CopilotBillingHealth.ps1 runs the spending policy, group and member checks. Billing policies are still design only.

gets: A scored HTML report with a fix for every finding

posts.title: Introducing Copilot Group Assignment Guide
posts.summary: Scripts and steps that create the Copilot groups, access packages and PIM admin groups, and say which admin center setting each group goes in.
posts.purpose:
This guide shows where to use each Copilot group. The scripts in this folder create the groups. You add each group to its admin center setting one time. After that, you add or remove people with access packages, not in the admin centers.

Admin centers change often, and some options only appear in some tenants. If your screen doesn't match, trust your screen.
needs: Microsoft 365 Copilot with Copilot Cowork, if you run it there instead of PowerShell

Microsoft Graph permissions: AccessReview.ReadWrite.All, CopilotCostManagement.Read.All, EntitlementManagement.ReadWrite.All, Group.Read.All, Group.ReadWrite.All, PrivilegedAssignmentSchedule.ReadWrite.AzureADGroup, PrivilegedEligibilitySchedule.ReadWrite.AzureADGroup, RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory and 2 more
gets: Copilot access managed through groups, so you add or remove people in one place

posts.title: Introducing Second Brain Prompts for Microsoft Copilot Cowork
posts.summary: Scheduled Cowork prompts that read your meetings, Teams, email and public sources.
posts.purpose:
Prompts for scheduled AI agents that build a personal work "second brain" from Microsoft 365 data and public sources. Each prompt runs as a daily scheduled task and writes Markdown files to OneDrive.

Six collection jobs gather information. Job 10 runs last: it's the only job that writes to the action tracker, and it builds a single Daily Briefing page and sends a Teams chat with the highlights.
gets: A personal "second brain" of Markdown notes in OneDrive that Copilot can search
